title: Outage: checkout times out in a sale, and the third backend is not taking traffic

sources.cite: Linux Foundation Certified System Administrator (LFCS): Domains & Competencies, Networking 25%
sources.note: Relevant text: Networking, 'Implement reverse proxies and load balancers'. Read as the page's HTML on 2026-11-14 (page last modified 2026-10-30).

Relevant text: 'By default, requests are distributed between the servers using a weighted round-robin balancing method'; max_fails 'By default, the number of unsuccessful attempts is set to 1'; fail_timeout 'By default, the parameter is set to 10 seconds'; slow_start is listed under 'the following parameters are available as part of our commercial subscription'. Read through summarizing fetches 2026-11-14. The [emerg] message open-source nginx prints for slow_start is authored in nginx's style.

Relevant text: on HUP 'The master process first checks the syntax validity, then tries to apply new configuration ... If this fails, it rolls back changes and continues to work with old configuration. If this succeeds, it starts new worker processes, and sends messages to old worker processes requesting them to shut down gracefully.' Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-14. That a restart with an invalid configuration leaves nginx stopped follows from the stop happening before the failed start.

Relevant text: default 'proxy_next_upstream error timeout;'; error, 'an error occurred while establishing a connection with the server, passing a request to it, or reading the response header'. Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-14. So a pool member that refuses connections is skipped, not shown to customers: it adds no capacity, and only the error log says so.

brief.situation: You run lb1, the nginx load balancer for Fernhill Outdoor's online shop (fictional). A sale starts at 11:30; two backends, app1 and app2, are timing out on checkout. Yesterday the platform team built a third backend, app3 (10.0.0.13), and left a change ticket: add 'server 10.0.0.13:8080 slow_start=30s;' to the shop upstream. The sale email goes out at 12:00 and will double the traffic.
handover: The upstream is in /etc/nginx/conf.d/shop.conf. lb1 runs the open-source nginx package.
The shop service on app3 reads its listen address from /etc/shopapp/app.env.
howItWorks: Run commands from the command line: type one, or pick it from the suggestions or the action list. Only this lab's commands run; there is no free shell, and each command's arguments are fixed.
Each command takes operator time: run it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The outage keeps developing on the same clock.
The map shows each host, disk or service and the links between them, with a status in words. Output appears in the terminal as it happens.
When you declare the service restored, you write the incident record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: How many operator minutes each command takes, and when the fictional outage spreads, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values. The sale email goes out at 12:00, 30 minutes after the start.

writeup.question: For the incident record: why checkout timed out, why app3 took no traffic, and how you changed a live load balancer safely.

parts.label: Cause
parts.criteria: Names app1 and app2 overloaded, app3 listening on 127.0.0.1 only, and the ticket's slow_start parameter, which open-source nginx rejects.
parts.modelAnswer: Two backends could not carry the sale; app3 was built but bound to localhost, and the ticket's slow_start is a commercial-only parameter that makes the configuration invalid.

parts.label: Evidence
parts.criteria: Uses the error log, ss on app3 or a direct curl, and nginx -t before applying anything.
parts.modelAnswer: error.log showed upstream timeouts on app1 and app2; ss on app3 showed 127.0.0.1:8080; nginx -t rejected slow_start.

parts.label: Change
parts.criteria: Fixes app3's listen address, adds it without slow_start, passes nginx -t, then reloads (not restarts) and checks checkout; explains that a refused reload keeps the old configuration, while a refused restart stops nginx.
parts.modelAnswer: BIND=0.0.0.0 on app3, added 'server 10.0.0.13:8080;', nginx -t passed, systemctl reload nginx; the 504s stopped. A restart with the ticket's line would have stopped nginx and taken the whole shop down.

expertPath.text: error.log: upstream timeouts on app1 and app2. Before adding app3, check it: ss on app3 shows 127.0.0.1:8080.
Set BIND=0.0.0.0 on app3 and restart its service; curl app3's health check from lb1.
Add the server line; nginx -t rejects slow_start (commercial only), so drop it; nginx -t passes.
systemctl reload nginx, curl checkout for a 200, and tell the platform team the ticket's line needs editing.

fixed.headline: Good: third backend serving
fixed.body: You checked app3 before trusting it, caught the commercial-only parameter with nginx -t, and reloaded so nothing in flight was lost.

fixedGaps.headline: Serving, with gaps
fixedGaps.body: app3 is in. The criteria show what it cost: time, a change applied untested, or no look first.

lbStopped.headline: The whole shop went down
lbStopped.body: A reload on an invalid configuration is refused and nginx keeps running the old one; a restart stops nginx first and then fails to start it. Test with nginx -t, then reload.

stillFailing.headline: Closed too soon
stillFailing.body: A pool member that refuses connections is skipped quietly: customers never see app3's errors, only the error log does.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Timeouts on app1 and app2 mean too little capacity, and app3 exists. Check it before adding it: ss shows it bound to 127.0.0.1, so fix the bind. The ticket's slow_start is a commercial-subscription parameter; nginx -t rejects it. With the plain line and a passing test, reload: workers swap gracefully, and a refused reload would have kept the old configuration, whereas a restart on a bad file stops nginx.
